issues.legal_issue: The amended tenancy protections apply to a tenancy already in existence when the amendment took effect if the tenancy had not yet expired and the landlord’s right to obtain possession had not yet accrued.
material_facts: The lease had been statutorily extended and was due to expire after the amendment took effect.
The amendment provided for further automatic renewal of the tenancy unless it was terminated in the prescribed manner.
The landlord sought possession after the amendment took effect.
issues.conclusion: The amendment applied to the existing tenancy prospectively, and the tenancy was extended unless terminated in accordance with the amended statutory requirements.
issues.legal_principle: The amended Section 5(1) of the Bombay Tenancy and Agricultural Lands Act, 1948 provided for successive renewals, subject to the statutory provisions governing termination; the amended Section 5(2) prescribed the landlord’s method of termination, and Section 5(3) addressed other grounds for termination and surrender. A statute operating in the future is not retrospective merely because it affects existing rights. The Court applied West v. Gwynne and Durlabhai Fakirbhai v. Jhaverbhai Bhikabhai, and noted that Jivabhai Purshottam v. Chhagan Karson approved the approach in Durlabhai.

predicates.tenancy_ejectment_proceeding: A landlord brought a proceeding seeking to recover possession from a tenant.
predicates.tenancy_existed_when_change_began: The tenancy was in existence when the legal change took effect.
predicates.tenancy_had_not_expired_when_change_bega: The tenancy had not expired, and the landlord’s right to obtain possession had not accrued, when the legal change took effect.

issues.definition: When a landlord seeks possession in a proceeding involving a tenancy that was still in existence when the legal change took effect, the new tenancy protection applies.

issues.legal_issue: A landlord’s right to obtain possession accrues when the tenancy expires, not merely when the landlord gives notice, so a notice given before the change cannot support eviction after the change unless it meets the requirements then applicable.
material_facts: The landlord gave notice before the amendment, stating that the tenancy would end when its then-scheduled term expired.
The tenancy was due to expire after the amendment took effect, which imposed additional requirements for a landlord’s notice terminating the tenancy.
The earlier notice did not include the required grounds, and the landlord sought possession on the basis of that notice.
issues.conclusion: The earlier notice did not entitle the landlord to possession; the landlord had to comply with the amended statutory requirements for a valid notice.
issues.legal_principle: Under the amended Section 5(2) of the Bombay Tenancy and Agricultural Lands Act, 1948, a landlord could terminate the tenancy only by giving the prescribed notice and satisfying the specified grounds. The landlord’s right to obtain possession accrued when the tenancy actually expired, not when notice was given. The Court applied Durlabhai Fakirbhai v. Jhaverbhai Bhikabhai, whose reasoning was approved in Jivabhai Purshottam v. Chhagan Karson, and distinguished the prospective operation discussed in Sakharam alias Bapusaheb Narayan Sanas v. Manikchand Motichand Shah as not analogous.

rule.if: tenancy_ejectment_proceeding and notice_preceded_legal_change and tenancy_expired_after_legal_change and notice_lacked_then_applicable_requirements

predicates.tenancy_ejectment_proceeding: A landlord brought a proceeding seeking to recover possession from a tenant.
predicates.notice_preceded_legal_change: The landlord gave notice before the legal change took effect.
predicates.tenancy_expired_after_legal_change: The tenancy was due to expire after the legal change took effect.
predicates.notice_lacked_then_applicable_requiremen: The notice did not satisfy the requirements applicable when the tenancy expired.

issues.definition: If a landlord seeks possession after a tenancy expires following a legal change, a notice given before that change does not support eviction when it lacks the requirements applicable at expiry.
